messages:
Priya: Heads-up — customer requested clarifications on RBAC scoping, audit log exports, and BYOK/KMS proofs as part of their security questionnaire. Can we assemble a concise answer set before their call tomorrow?
Ben: I can pull the current RBAC matrix + roles doc. Which export format do they want for audit logs? CSV/JSON/SIEM syslog?
Priya: They asked for SIEM-compatible export and signed log snapshots for a one-week window. Also want assurance that service accounts can't escalate to tenant resources.
Lena: For the SIEM side we have the logshipper pipeline that forwards to customer endpoints or to our S3 staging with signed manifests. It supports JSONlines and syslog over TLS.
Carlos: Quick note: the signed snapshots we provide are HMACed by our audit-service using the rotation key in KMS. We can produce a time-bounded bundle.
Maya: @Lena can you confirm retention windows and whether we can provide a hashed line-level redaction option? Customer is sensitive about PII leaking.
Lena: Retention: default 90 days in hot store, 365 days in cold. Redaction: we support configurable field filters at shipper time. We can supply sample command to extract only metadata fields.
Ben: For RBAC scoping — we enforce least privilege: tenant-admin role is scoped to tenant_id, service accounts are namespaced and need specific `tenant:write` grants to mutate tenant resources. No cross-tenant escalation path exists in prod.
Priya: Good. They specifically asked for proof: an example of a minimal service-account policy + a short runbook showing how we audit role changes.
Carlos: I can export a sanitized example policy file:
```
{
  "service_account": "sa-ingest-123",
  "permissions": ["tenant:read","ingest:write"],
  "scope": "tenant:acme-corp"
}
```
And the runbook snippet: `audit-service query --start 2026-03-01 --end 2026-03-07 --resource tenant:acme-corp --output signed-bundle.tar.gz`
Maya: About BYOK: customer wants to know whether keys are in their HSM or if we hold key material. We should be explicit: for Private deployments they can provide a KMS endpoint (HSM-backed) we never import keys into our control plane. For Hosted we manage envelope keys but offer CMEK by request with a contract.
Priya: Can you add the nuance that we also support key-escrow+rotate for Dedicated contracts? Some procurement teams ask that.
Lena: Adding: Dedicated customers may opt for dual control escrow where the key material is split with a partner HSM — optional.
Ben: One more ask from the questionnaire: timeline and contacts for incident response if a suspicious RBAC change is detected. We should include an oncall flow + SLA for acknowledgement.
Priya: I'll draft: 15m ack for Sev1, 1hr initial investigation update, postmortem under our IR cadence. Include PagerDuty escalation and a direct sec-oncall email.
sec-bot: Incident policy link: https://redwood.internal/policies/incident-response (read-only).
Carlos: For the signed log proof, note caveat: snapshots prove log integrity from our ingestion point; they don't prove operations inside a tenant-managed external KMS. We should call that out so customers don't conflate guarantees.
Maya: Agree. Also add a short Q&A: "Can Redwood rotate tenant keys?" -> For BYOK: customer rotates keys; for hosted with CMEK we provide rotation on request.
Priya: OK action items: @Ben prepare RBAC matrix + sample policy, @Lena prepare log export options + retention table + redaction examples, @Carlos prepare signed-snapshot example and one-sentence caveats, @Maya write BYOK/CMEK wording. I'll assemble answers and slide for tomorrow's call.
Ben: On it, will drop artifacts to /shared/sec/acme-qna by EOD.
Lena: I'll attach sample curl to ship logs to SIEM: `curl -X POST https://logs.redwood.io/ship -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" --data-binary @snapshot.json`
Maya: I'll ping legal for a short blurb on escrow options.
Priya: Thanks all — if anything is blocking call me. :thumbsup:
